data.title: Rivian vs. Lucid: Which EV Stock Is the Better Buy After Their YTD Plunge?
data.description:
Shares of U.S. electric vehicle maker Rivian (RIVN) are down roughly 50% since the start of the year to about $11.71. Its rival Lucid (LCID) is worse off, with shares down about 76% year-to-date. This comes as both EV makers are still racing to turn a net profit. On Wall Street, analysts are more bullish on Rivian, but Lucid offers the bigger upside of about 128%.

Why Rivian and Lucid Shares Have Sold Off This Year

Rivian shares have sold off this year as the automaker continues to burn cash and post losses. In the third quarter, net loss was $913 million. The EV maker used up $1.12 billion in free cash flow during the quarter.

This took the shine off its revenue, which rose 38% year-over-year to $2.2 billion. Rivian posted record quarterly deliveries of 19,248 units during the period. Demand for the R2, its new and more affordable SUV, drove revenue growth.

Likewise, shares have fallen as its EV credits have dried up due to changes in federal policy. In addition to the R2’s lower prices, this development hurt the automaker’s automotive gross margin in the third quarter.

Notably, Lucid shares also faced pressure amid recent bankruptcy rumors that the company promptly denied.

Why Analysts Like Rivian Better

Analysts are more bullish on Rivian than Lucid. Seaport Global analyst Ronald Jewsikow recently called RIVN stock a Buy. He sees room for the stock to gain beyond Rivian’s planned vehicle lineup. 

Five-star Jefferies analyst Philippe Houchois also recently upgraded Rivian shares from Hold to Buy. He pointed to demand for the R2. According to Houchois, Rivian converted more customer preorders for the high-end R2 launch trim into actual sales than it expected.

By contrast, Jewsikow started coverage of Lucid with a Sell rating. He argued that the EV maker would need significant capital to develop and launch the three new midsize vehicles it is planning.

Meanwhile, four-star Baird analyst Ben Kallo recently maintained his Hold rating on Lucid. However, Kallo noted that Lucid’s efforts to reduce expenses are beginning to show results. He also pointed to the carmaker’s progress in developing its self-driving technology.

Which EV Stock Is the Better Buy?

As mentioned earlier, Rivian (RIVN) has the better consensus analyst rating: a Moderate Buy. However, TipRanks’ Stock Comparison tool shows that Lucid (LCID) offers the bigger upside of about 128%.
data.author: Solomon Oladipupo

data.title: Retail Stocks to Watch as the Battle for $1 Trillion in Holiday Sales Intensifies
data.description:
U.S. retailers are racing to cross $1 trillion in holiday sales for the first time this year. Notably, many see Thanksgiving Day on Thursday as the start of the U.S. holiday and shopping season. Black Friday sales start tomorrow, November 27, followed by Cyber Monday on November 30. As a result, the race to capture holiday sales has begun in earnest. Several retail stocks are worth watching, including Amazon (AMZN), Walmart (WMT), and Costco (COST).

  • Amazon (AMZN) — Amazon is the world’s largest company by sales. It generated $716.9 billion in net sales in 2025, up by 12% from $638 billion the previous year. That number is expected to rise 25% to $892.2 billion this year. Beyond its cloud business, Amazon is also an e-commerce giant. It sells goods online and offers other merchants a place to sell. According to Bernstein analyst Zhihan Ma, Amazon and Walmart are “the most obvious e-commerce destinations” among shoppers. Amazon has said it is expanding its Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals to 12 days. This is the largest such extension in the company’s history.
  • Walmart (WMT) — Walmart is the world’s second-largest company by sales. It was recently overtaken by Amazon. In fiscal 2026 (which ended in January 2026), its sales rose 4.7% to $713.2 billion. In October, Walmart announced early dates for Black Friday and Cyber Monday. It also recently launched a program to help members save $100 yearly. Telsey Advisory Group analysts have said that Walmart “should be another winner this holiday season.”
  • Costco (COST) — Costco is a big-box retailer known for offering quality bulk purchases at the lowest prices possible. Analysts have continued to praise the retailer’s ability to compete on pricing. During fiscal 2026, which ended in August, Costco’s net sales reached $269.9 billion, up 10.2% from the previous year. Sales have continued to rise afterward.
  • Target (TGT) — Target is a discount and general merchandise retailer. The company’s efforts to improve sales are starting to pay off. About a week ago, Target reported its third-quarter 2026 sales. It posted its strongest growth in more than five years.
  • Best Buy (BBY) — Best Buy is an electronics and appliances retailer. The company’s business has been under pressure as chip shortages forced producers to raise the prices of electronic products. Still, Best Buy reported its best same-store sales in five years this week. It also raised its fiscal 2027 sales forecast.

Which Retail Stock Is the Best Buy?

Of the retail stocks highlighted in this article, Amazon (AMZN) stands out.

According to TipRanks’ Stock Comparison tool, Amazon carries a Strong Buy consensus rating and 33% upside. The upside is based on the average price target of $326.15.

data.title: ‘It Isn’t Coming,’ Says Investor About Micron Stock
data.description:
Micron (NASDAQ:MU) investors barely had time to enjoy some respite. Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO on Nov. 23, and chip stocks ripped higher on the news. The memory maker then handed back almost all of that gain over the next two sessions, after BNP Paribas downgraded the stock to Neutral and TrendForce trimmed its 2027 memory forecasts on order cuts from Chinese cloud providers.

U.S. markets are closed today for Thanksgiving, so the shares sit at Wednesday’s close of $601.25, roughly half their June 25 record close of $1,213.56.

So, where to now for this this until-recently high-flying stock? Well, according to a top investor using the pseudonym The Asian Investor (TAI), the market has this one wrong. In TAI’s view, the selling has been driven by doubts about the AI boom and about debt-funded spending by neocloud providers, not by anything going wrong inside Micron’s business. The valuation now reflects a level of gloom that the fundamentals don’t support.

Micron trades at about 3.4x forward earnings, and peers SK hynix and Sandisk are even cheaper at roughly 2x to 2.5x. According to TAI, multiples this low only make sense if investors expect profits to slump within the next two or three years. The investor doesn’t see that happening and argues the current price leaves plenty of room for error.

The case rests on high-bandwidth memory (HBM), the chips that sit beside AI processors in data centers. TrendForce expects HBM to take up about 30% of the industry’s DRAM wafer capacity in 2027, up from around 22% this year. Every wafer that goes to HBM is one less for regular DRAM, which keeps supply tight across the board. TrendForce also projects that blended HBM prices will rise 121% year over year in 2027. Micron says much of its 2027 HBM supply is already spoken for, at prices well above this year’s, and it is scaling up HBM4 production. TAI, who ranks among the top 4% of investors on TipRanks, adds that agentic AI tools need far more memory than earlier AI workloads, which could stretch the shortage out for years.

The next test is the fiscal first-quarter report on Dec. 17. Wall Street expects adjusted EPS of about $38.20, compared with $4.78 a year earlier, a jump of roughly 700% YoY, and analysts have been raising their estimates ahead of the release.

The main risk, in TAI’s view, is that the HBM boom fades the way memory cycles usually do. If AI spending stalls, Micron would have to accept lower prices for its DRAM and HBM, and its gross margin would shrink with them. For now, the investor sees hyperscalers raising their capital budgets while their sales keep growing, which suggests the AI spending is paying off. Micron’s own management expects supply to be tighter in 2027 and 2028 than it is now.

“With a positive earnings trend, leading gross profit growth (on a TTM basis) in the industry group, triple-digit earnings growth, and a favorable EPS estimate revision trend three weeks before earnings, I see not only a strong earnings report but also a major revaluation catalyst ahead for investors,” the 5-star investor summed up.

Accordingly, TAI has made Micron the biggest memory bet in the portfolio and rates the stock a Strong Buy. (To watch TAI’s track record, click here)

That is also the conclusion reached by the analyst consensus, a rating based on 28 Buys and 2 Holds. Going by the $1,574 average price target, a year from now, shares will be changing hands for a 162% premium. (See MU stock forecast)

data.title: SpaceX vs. Rocket Lab: One Space Stock Is a Buy, the Other Isn’t Worth the Price, Says Mizuho
data.description:
Getting a satellite into orbit has never been cheaper, but owning the companies that put them there has cost investors plenty this year. SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB) both ran hard into SpaceX’s June IPO and have spent much of the time since handing those gains back. Space stocks still move as a pack, so a rough day for one usually drags the rest along.

Wednesday showed how jumpy the trade is. SpaceX opened sharply lower on Wednesday and at one point was down about 9% from Tuesday’s close as the cost of insuring its debt hit a record and investors pushed back on a possible tie-up with Tesla. It recovered after the FCC approved its plan for up to 1 million satellites working as orbital data centers, closing at $127.44, about 37% below its June record close. Rocket Lab ended the day at $47.02, roughly 69% off its May peak, with the first flight of its Neutron rocket now pushed into 2027. U.S. markets are closed today for Thanksgiving.

Mizuho analyst Greg Konrad recently launched coverage of the space sector and is upbeat on the industry, but he thinks the theme alone isn’t enough. What matters, in his view, is whether a company delivers and what investors are paying for it.

SpaceX

Konrad sees SpaceX as the best example in the group of a company that does everything in-house. Reusable rockets have brought its launch costs down by roughly 85% to 90% compared with the historical average, and everything else is built on that cheap ride. Falcon and Starship carry Starlink satellites into orbit, Starlink brings in the money, and the AI arm, built around xAI and the Colossus compute clusters, is where the analyst sees the biggest potential payoff.

Starlink is the part that’s already proven. It generated $11.4 billion in revenue in 2025 at an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 63%. The next step is the V3 satellite, which Konrad says puts about 20 times as much bandwidth into orbit on each launch. That should let Starlink go after crowded cities that older satellites couldn’t serve well. V3s fly on Starship, which reached orbit for the first time on Sept. 28 and released 26 of them.

The growth Konrad is modeling is enormous: revenue up 201% year over year in 2027, with AI revenue up 315%, connectivity up 70% and the space business up 54%.

The flip side to that is spending. Heavy investment in AI and Starship has pushed free cash flow below zero even as EBITDA grows. He also flags Starship’s timeline, the cost of the AI buildout, governance, and the flood of shares coming out of lockup, with the final IPO tranche unlocking on Dec. 8. Still, Konrad thinks owning the rockets, the network and the compute gives SpaceX an edge no one else can match.

“SpaceX is the ultimate vertical integration play,” he said, rating the stock as Outperform. His $205 price target implies shares will gain 61% in the months ahead. (To watch Konrad’s track record, click here)

Most of Konrad’s colleagues agree with that stance. With an additional 27 Buys, 6 Holds and 1 Sell, the stock claims a Strong Buy consensus rating. At $265, the average price target implies shares will gain 108% over the 12-month timeframe. (See SPCX stock forecast)

Rocket Lab

Rocket Lab is a tougher call for Konrad, and the business isn’t the reason. He likes the company, and of the space names he covers, it has the clearest view of future revenue.

That is contingent on three things happening: more frequent Electron launches, Neutron’s planned ramp from one flight to three and then five a year, and a Space Systems unit that is graduating from selling parts to leading whole spacecraft programs. Space Systems already brought in about two-thirds of 2025 revenue. The pending Iridium deal, expected to close by mid-2027, would add a fourth leg of recurring revenue, though Konrad doesn’t expect the bigger synergies until after 2030.

Demand isn’t the issue either. Few companies can reliably reach orbit, launch slots are scarce, and the backlog hit an all-time high of $3.57 billion at the end of September.

The sticking point is valuation. Konrad expects revenue to grow 29% in 2027 and 36% in 2028, which puts Rocket Lab right around the middle of the space group. Yet on forward revenue, the stock is valued at a steep premium to its peers, SpaceX included.

Investors, in other words, are already paying for growth he sees as fairly average. With Neutron’s debut slipping and Iridium’s biggest payoff not due until the next decade, there isn’t much room for error.

“We like the business, but struggle with the valuation,” Konrad said. He values the shares at 10.5 times 2028 pro forma EV/revenue and rates Rocket Lab as Underperform (i.e., Sell) with a $40 price target. That figure implies shares will fall another 15% over the next year.

Konrad, however, is the Street’s lone RKLB bear. Elsewhere, an additional 15 Buys and 3 Holds all add up to a Moderate Buy consensus view. The forecast calls for 12-month returns of 96%, given the average price target clocks in at $92.33. (See RKLB stock forecast)

data.title: 13F Filings Show Big Investors Bought the Sandisk Stock Dip. It Kept Dipping. Time to Load Up?
data.description:
U.S. markets are closed for Thanksgiving on Thursday, a break for Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) shareholders after another rough session. The flash memory maker fell again on Wednesday after TrendForce said demand for NAND chips in China looks even weaker than it had thought. Chinese cloud companies can’t get enough GPUs, so they need less of the storage that goes with them. That followed the research firm’s warning last week that NAND contract prices will start falling early next year.

Sandisk closed Wednesday at $73.61, down about 5.5% on the day. The stock has more than halved over the past month and sits about 75% below its June 25 record close, adjusted for the 8-for-1 stock split that took effect last week.

The latest 13F filings, which show holdings as of Sept. 30, reveal that most big investors were buying. Sandisk had fallen about 23% during the third quarter, and many funds used the drop to add shares. The share counts below are from before the split.

The largest single move, though, was a sale. Leopold Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness sold all 2.5 million of its Sandisk shares. At the end of June, that stake was worth $5.67 billion, the fund’s biggest holding at 28% of the stocks it reported. The fund kept some exposure through call options with a notional value of $183 million. The sale was part of a forced unwind after July’s AI selloff hit the heavily leveraged fund with margin calls. Stanley Druckenmiller’s Duquesne Family Office also sold out, unloading 34,900 shares worth about $79 million at the end of June.

Jericho Capital made the biggest purchase, opening a stake of 391,880 shares worth $682 million on Sept. 30. Renaissance Technologies increased its position more than 55-fold, from 4,980 shares to 276,460, worth $481 million. GQG Partners opened a $210 million stake, Brad Gerstner’s Altimeter Capital started a smaller position of 25,170 shares, and Bridgewater Associates went from just 317 shares to 66,756, worth about $116 million.

By 13Foresight’s count, 1,192 funds opened or added to Sandisk positions in the quarter, against 870 that trimmed or sold out. Any of them that held on are sitting on steep losses, since the stock is now about two-thirds below its Sept. 30 price. The filings don’t show whether they’ve sold since.

On the Street, the NAND flash specialist still gets plenty of support. Based on 12 Buys and 3 Holds, the analyst consensus rates the stock a Strong Buy. At $252.06, the average price target implies shares will gain 242% in the months ahead. (See SNDK stock forecast)

data.title: 3 Vanguard Sector ETFs That Give Investors an Edge
data.description:
Vanguard offers a wide range of sector ETFs that give investors exposure to different parts of the U.S. stock market. Some focus on steady demand for everyday products and the energy sector, while others target technology companies with strong growth potential. Using TipRanks’ Best Vanguard ETFs tool, three Vanguard ETFs stand out: Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE), Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC), and Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT).

VDE invests in energy companies, VDC focuses on consumer staples companies, while VGT holds major technology stocks.

According to TipRanks’ unique ETF Analyst Consensus, which is based on a weighted average of analyst ratings for each ETF’s holdings, VGT has a Strong Buy rating. Based on analysts’ price targets, VGT’s average price target of $150.69 offers the highest upside of over 45%. It invests in tech companies that are growing fast. These companies also benefit from rising demand for AI and cloud services.

Meanwhile, VDC and VDE carry Moderate Buy ratings. VDE offers upside of 24%, and VDC offers 7%. Energy stocks are sensitive to changes in oil and gas prices, while consumer staples companies generally see slower growth due to steady demand for everyday products.

Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC)

The Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) invests in consumer defensive companies. These companies sell everyday essentials like food, beverages, and household goods. Because demand for these products stays steady even during economic slowdowns, VDC is often seen as a defensive ETF with lower volatility. It has a beta of 0.25.

The fund has 95.4% of its holdings in the consumer defensive sector. It also offers a dividend yield of 1.94% with a quarterly dividend of $1.21 per share.

VDC owns 105 stocks with total assets of $8.3 billion. Its top holdings include major consumer brands such as Walmart (WMT), Costco Wholesale (COST), and Procter & Gamble (PG).

Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE)

The Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE) offers broad exposure to the U.S. energy sector. VDE holds stocks involved in oil and gas exploration, production, refining, equipment services, and midstream infrastructure. The ETF has historically performed well when oil prices rise and can also help protect against inflation.

The fund has 99.19% of its holdings in the energy sector. VDE has historically offered a higher dividend yield than the broader market. VDE has a dividend yield of 2.31% and pays a $1.05 quarterly dividend.

Its top 3 holdings are Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), Chevron (CVX), and ConocoPhillips (COP). Overall, VDE holds 113 stocks with total assets worth $9.93 billion.

Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT)

Vanguard Information Technology ETF is focused solely on U.S. technology stocks, with major holdings including Nvidia (NVDA), Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Broadcom (AVGO), and Micron (MU). The ETF has 99.38% of its holdings in the technology sector. VGT has 316 stocks with total assets of $133.08 billion.

The fund’s narrow focus can lead to bigger swings than broader market funds. With a beta of 1.49, the ETF tends to be more volatile, and its expense ratio of 0.09% is slightly higher than some diversified alternatives.

data.title: SpaceX vs. Tesla: What Sets Them Apart, and Could They Merge?
data.description:
Elon Musk leads two companies with very different goals. SpaceX (SPCX) builds rockets and runs an internet service from space, while Tesla (TSLA) makes electric cars and sells power storage systems. Each has its own path to growth, but a possible merger has raised new questions for investors.

The prospect of a merger has drawn fresh interest. On November 24, the Financial Times reported that Tesla and SpaceX had named five board members to lead talks. The report said the firms were looking at a possible $3.5 trillion all-stock deal. The two firms have yet to announce a deal, and the terms remain open.

SpaceX: A Leader in Space and Satellite Internet

SpaceX has built its name by launching rockets and sending gear into space. The company also builds Starship, a large rocket meant to carry heavy loads into space. SpaceX also won the first U.S. approval to launch up to 1 million satellites for AI data centers in space.

Starlink, its satellite web service, is a key source of cash. Reusable rockets have cut launch costs by 85% to 90%, while Starlink had $11.4 billion in 2025 sales and 10.3 million users.

Recently, Mizuho Securities analyst Brett Linzey started coverage of SpaceX with a Buy rating and $205 price target. He sees growth in space, Starlink and AI, but flags high costs, Starship delays and risks tied to future share sales.

Tesla: More Than an EV Company?

Tesla is best known for its electric vehicles, such as the Model 3 and Model Y. It also sells home and grid power storage systems. Its main car unit faces stiff price pressure as more companies enter the EV market. Tesla is also investing millions into self-driving technology, AI, and robots.

Seaport Global analyst Ronald Jewsikow began coverage of Tesla with a Buy rating and a $475 price target. He sees robotaxis as the main source of future growth and expects annual sales to reach $3 billion to $4 billion by the end of 2027. Jewsikow also expects car sales and margins to rise in 2027. While Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Waymo remains his pick for market lead in 2030, he sees scope for Tesla to gain ground.

Could SpaceX and Tesla Merge?

A Tesla-SpaceX merger would raise key questions about the value of each company, the share swap terms, and who would hold control. Tesla shareholders could gain exposure to space and satellite web services, but they would also take on the costs and risks of those businesses.

RBC Capital analyst Ken Herbert sees a merger as a real chance by early 2027, sooner than he had expected. He also said Tesla may get a price above its fair value, but some investors may accept a deal without a large premium. Herbert reiterated his Buy ratings on both companies.

Which Stock Does Wall Street Prefer?

According to TipRanks Stock Comparison Tool, SpaceX currently has a Strong Buy consensus rating while Tesla has a Moderate Buy. SpaceX’s average analyst price target implies a higher upside of nearly 108%, compared with 8% for Tesla.
data.author: Sheryl Sheth

data.title: 3 High-Yield Dividend Stocks to Watch This Thanksgiving
data.description:
Thanksgiving is a good time to review income investments through Dividend Stocks. Three stocks stand out for their high yields: Frontline (FRO), Nordic American Tankers (NAT), and Ares Capital (ARCC). All three pay dividends, but their income profiles differ. Based on TipRanks data, their indicated yields range from about 10% to 13%.

Frontline (FRO)

Frontline operates oil tankers, transporting crude oil and petroleum products. Its earnings depend heavily on shipping rates, which can rise or fall quickly.

The company has a record of quarterly dividends, but payments have varied widely. Its latest declared regular quarterly dividend is $2.38 per share, reflecting a current yield of 12.97%. In 2025, regular quarterly dividends totaled just $0.93, highlighting the risk of relying on peak-cycle payouts.

TipRanks reports a Moderate Buy consensus rating on FRO. The average analyst price target of $58.07 implies 21.9% upside from the November 25 closing price of $47.65.

Nordic American Tankers (NAT)

Nordic American Tankers operates a fleet of Suezmax oil tankers. Its business is exposed to the same freight-rate cycle as Frontline.

NAT paid a dividend of $0.27 per share in its latest reported quarter, implying a current yield of 12.19%. The company has paid quarterly dividends, but the amounts have changed significantly. For example, payments rose from $0.10 in September 2025 to $0.27 in September 2026.

On TipRanks, NAT has a Hold consensus rating with an average analyst price target of $8.50 implying 31.2% upside from the November 25 closing price.

Ares Capital (ARCC)

Ares Capital is a U.S. specialty finance company that lends money to mid-sized businesses. It is not a traditional bank or an asset management company. Its income comes largely from its investment portfolio rather than shipping rates.

ARCC has maintained a $0.48 quarterly dividend throughout 2024, 2025, and 2026. That equals $1.92 annually, with a yield of 10.13%. Its dividend record is more stable than those of the tanker companies, although credit losses could still affect future payments.

On TipRanks, ARCC has a Strong Buy consensus rating with the average analyst price target of $20.42 implying 7.7% upside from the November 25 closing price.

data.title: 3 Space Stocks with 95%+ Upside Potential, According to Analysts
data.description:

A growth stock is a company whose sales and earnings are expected to grow faster than the broader market. Investors buy growth stocks mainly for share-price gains.

Planet Labs (PL)

Planet Labs uses satellites to take images of Earth. It sells this data to businesses and governments for tasks such as mapping, farming, and defense. The company is expanding its business to meet rising demand for satellite images and data. It is also investing in new satellite technology and AI tools that could open up new ways to make money. However, PL stock is down more than 45% year-to-date.

Analysts have rated Planet Labs’ stock as a Moderate Buy, backed by eight Buys and three Holds assigned in the last three months. Meanwhile, PL’s average stock price target of $30.0 suggests a potential upside of over 180% from current levels.

Intuitive Machines (LUNR)

Intuitive Machines builds lunar landers and provides services for NASA and other customers. It is considered a growth stock because it aims to expand its business through more Moon missions and new space contracts. However, its growth depends on mission success and winning new deals.

LUNR stock has a Strong Buy rating based on eight Buys and one Sell assigned in the last three months. LUNR stock’s average price target of $26.33 implies an upside potential of over 185%.

Rocket Lab (RKLB)

Rocket Lab builds rockets and spacecraft and provides launch services. Its reusable medium-lift rocket, Neutron, is expected to launch in 2027 and could be a key catalyst for the stock. Its planned acquisition of Iridium (IRDM) could also give the company a larger revenue base.

data.title: Top Guggenheim Analyst Upgrades CrowdStrike Stock (CRWD) to Buy After Zscaler Mega-Deal
data.description:
Guggenheim upgraded CrowdStrike (CRWD) stock to Buy from Neutral, setting a $280 price target and implying nearly 34% upside from Wednesday’s closing price of $209.30. The move follows CrowdStrike’s Fiscal Q3 2027 earnings report and its $43.9 billion all-stock agreement to acquire Zscaler (ZS), which weighed on shares earlier this week. Shares were down 8.92% to $208.97 on Monday before stabilizing midweek.

Guggenheim Sees Hyper Growth and Profit Ahead

Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci wrote that CrowdStrike’s execution track record justifies its valuation multiple and positions the company for “hyper growth and profit.” He also pointed to CrowdStrike’s partnerships with major cloud providers. Microsoft (MSFT), long viewed by investors as a direct rival, works closely with the company, as does Amazon (AMZN), specifically AWS.

DiFucci incorporated the Zscaler transaction into his updated model, noting that management expects the combined business to generate accretive organic growth by uniting CrowdStrike’s endpoint security platform with Zscaler’s network security and Zero Trust architecture. Still, he emphasized that the acquisition itself was not the primary reason for the upgrade.

Wall Street Reacts to Record Q3 Results and the Zscaler Deal

CrowdStrike’s upgrade followed its Fiscal Q3 2027 report on November 23, in which revenue rose 28% year-over-year to $1.58 billion, ending annual recurring revenue (ARR) grew 27% to $6.26 billion, and net new ARR reached a record $419.2 million. Alongside earnings, CrowdStrike announced an all-stock agreement to acquire Zscaler at 1.135 CRWD shares per ZS share, expected to close in the second half of Fiscal 2028.

Other firms also updated their ratings and targets on November 24:

data.title: ‘It’s Not Huang,’ Says Investor About Nvidia Stock
data.description:
Getting Jensen Huang back was supposed to end the drama at Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA). The board reinstated him as CEO on Monday, eleven days after he resigned, and the stock surged. The mood soured soon after. On Wednesday, S&P Global Ratings put the chipmaker’s AA credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade, citing weaknesses in management and governance. Nvidia also hasn’t yet filed its third-quarter 10-Q, which is due Dec. 4, and the Wall Street Journal has reported that the SEC is looking into whether the company’s disclosures misled investors.

Markets are closed for Thanksgiving, so the stock stands at $149.30 after Wednesday’s close. That’s about 37.5% under its early-October record close.

While the leadership saga has been driving sentiment around Nvidia and chip stocks in general, investor Rafa F. Oliver sees it as just a sideshow. In his view, Huang’s return moved the share price but did nothing for the cash the business generates. The bigger worry is how much of Nvidia’s demand the company now funds itself.

Nvidia has been backing its own buyers with equity stakes, long payment terms and guarantees. Management expects the major frontier labs to bring in about 15% of data center revenue this year, and the investor notes that every one of them has taken Nvidia money or guarantees. He estimates that customers with some form of Nvidia support will produce $173 billion, or 28%, of fiscal 2028 revenue. Roughly $65 billion of that wouldn’t exist without the support.

Then there are commitments Nvidia hasn’t paid yet. It carries up to $118 billion in guarantees. The biggest is $105 billion behind OpenAI’s lease at the PORTS-Pike campus in Ohio, and on top of that sits $32 billion of possible capacity purchases from neoclouds. Citing the 10-Q, Oliver says Nvidia stays on the hook until OpenAI earns a satisfactory credit rating. Customers are also paying more slowly: receivables have reached 64 days of sales, the highest since the 2022 chip slump.

Oliver calls the risk he sees a “financing shock.” In that scenario, lenders back away from cash-burning AI clouds and labs, or those businesses stumble, and Nvidia’s revenue, stakes and guarantees all suffer together. He puts the odds at 60%.

Even without a shock, he expects growth to slow. He models 49% revenue growth in fiscal 2028, against management’s outlook of about 75%. That gives revenue of $625.5 billion, compared with the $703 billion consensus he cites. He also uses a higher discount rate of 13.05%, because Nvidia’s sales now depend on AI spending that drives the whole market.

On paper, Nvidia doesn’t look pricey, trading at about 16 times trailing earnings. Oliver isn’t convinced the number tells the whole story. Much of what sits behind those earnings, from the receivables to the stakes and guarantees, hinges on customers that are still burning cash. When fourth-quarter results land in late February, the first things he’ll look at are how long customers are taking to pay and what has happened to the neocloud commitments.

For now, he rates the stock a Sell. (To watch Oliver’s track record, click here)

On the Street, however, only one analyst agrees with that take. With an additional 34 Buys and 9 Holds, the stock claims a Strong Buy consensus view. Going by the $234 average price target, a year from now, investors will be pocketing returns of 57%. (See NVDA stock forecast)

data.title: ‘Room to Spare,’ Says Investor About Oracle Stock
data.description:
For most of this year, the big question around Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) was whether it could pay for its data center ambitions. The company now says it can. In a Nov. 20 statement, it said all the funding for its OpenAI contract is in place. That message, along with Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia, sent the stock sharply higher on Monday. The rally didn’t last. A broad AI selloff on Tuesday and Wednesday wiped out the gains, and Oracle goes into the Thanksgiving break close to the 52-week low it hit midweek.

At about $104, the shares sit roughly 68% below their September 2025 record close.

Investor Louis Gerard still sees the balance sheet as the main problem. He just thinks it has become a smaller one. At its Oct. 28 Investor Day, Oracle promised to limit new capital raised through FY30 to $20 billion, half stock and half debt, and on Nov. 2 it raised the whole amount. Together with the $20 billion stock program it finished in the fiscal first quarter, that brings outside funding for fiscal 2027 to about $40 billion, which is what management said to expect back in June. For Gerard, a fixed limit is easier to live with than a funding need nobody can size.

The money came at a cost. Shareholders were diluted by 86 million new shares sold at $116. Oracle had also said in June that it didn’t plan to raise more debt in 2026, and that turned out to be wrong. Borrowing got more expensive too. Notes due 2029 yielded about 4.6% when Oracle sold them in February, compared with roughly 7% this month. The ratings agencies still have Oracle at investment grade, but bond buyers are charging it rates closer to junk.

The cap only covers the stock and bond markets. Until free cash flow turns positive, which Oracle expects in the second half of FY28, vendor financing and customer prepayments have to fill the gap. Prepayments made the first quarter look better than it was. Of the record $23.1 billion in operating cash flow, $11.4 billion came from customers paying in advance. Without that, free cash flow would have been about negative $16.8 billion instead of negative $5.4 billion.

Meanwhile, Gerard’s biggest worry is OpenAI. S&P estimates it accounts for about half of Oracle’s backlog. OpenAI’s latest round was also smaller and cheaper than it first wanted. CNBC reported $15 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation, against an original goal of $30 billion at $1.4 trillion.

Gerard sees power as a second risk. Oracle delivered 850 megawatts in the fiscal first quarter, short of the nearly 1 gigawatt it had pointed to. Hitting its goal of about 10 gigawatts by the end of FY28 means delivering about a gigawatt a quarter.

Even so, the valuation goes a long way for him. The stock trades at about 13 times the $8.10 in non-GAAP EPS Oracle expects for fiscal 2027, and about 5 times its FY30 target of $21 or more. If Oracle hits its goal of more than $30 billion in FY29 free cash flow, that would equal about 9% of its current market value. In Gerard’s view, the dilution, the costlier debt and the broken promise are already in the price, with “room to spare.”

Taking all that into account, Gerard has upgraded Oracle from Hold (i.e., Neutral) to Buy. (To watch Gerard’s track record, click here)

Most Street analysts agree with that assessment. Based on 28 Buys, 4 Holds and 1 Sell, the stock claims a Strong Buy consensus rating. Going by the $241.83 average price target, a year from now, shares will be changing hands for a 133% premium. (See ORCL stock forecast)

Analysts’ Views on PLTR

Lee called it “another extraordinary quarter” but remained cautious about the stock.

data.title: Take-Two’s (TTWO) GTA 6 Could Be a Cash Cow for the Next Decade
data.description:
Take-Two (TTWO) could have a cash cow for the next decade with Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6). The global video game publisher reported $3.79 billion in first-day retail sales for the title. Sam Houser, president of Take-Two’s game developer Rockstar Games, called the release “a new chapter of Rockstar Games.”

I think investors may still underestimate what that chapter could earn the company. The opening sales are extraordinary. An eventual PC release and online ecosystem could keep generating revenue long afterward. That prospect leaves me Bullish on TTWO stock.

An Extraordinary Launch Sets Up Q3

An extraordinary launch sets up a strong Fiscal Q3 for Take-Two. Rockstar reported 32.5 million units sold before release. Beyond the anticipation and hype, the game seems to be an extraordinary artistic achievement for the industry. Its Metacritic critic score was 99. Morgan Stanley (MS) said the launch exceeded already high expectations.

For perspective, GTA 5’s 2013 debut generated more than $800 million. GTA 6’s opening was roughly 4.7 times that figure at $3.79 billion. Even Disney’s (DIS) Avengers: Endgame’s global opening weekend reached $1.209 billion. The formats differ, but the scale of spending is remarkable.

I believe GTA 6 could become a generational benchmark. Game Informer’s review describes how small everyday encounters fit around elaborate criminal missions. The achievement appears to be coherence across an enormous, detailed world. I think we’ll still discuss how Rockstar accomplished that many years from now.

Few studios could fund such a project for over a decade. They would still need Rockstar’s technical skill and creative leadership. That makes this franchise exceptionally difficult to replicate.

The December-quarter earnings report should begin revealing the financial payoff. Management previously guided to $3.35–$3.50 billion of quarterly net bookings and $8.0–$8.2 billion for Fiscal 2027. Note that retail receipts are consumer spending. Bookings measure Take-Two’s net product and service sales. So GAAP revenue recognition can follow a different timetable.

Even allowing for those differences, I think year-end holiday demand creates room for higher guidance. I want to see updated unit figures and premium-edition adoption. Management’s roadmap for monetizing the installed player base will matter beyond the initial sales beat.

A Decade of Sales Could Follow

My thesis here is that a decade of exceptional sales figures could follow as Rockstar reaches new audiences. GTA 6 currently runs only on PlayStation 5 (PS5) and Xbox Series X/S. An eventual PC version could spark another substantial sales wave.

Also, future console versions could extend that further. Lower-priced editions would reach players who skipped the launch, while word of mouth can keep bringing people into a world worth exploring. GTA 5 has already demonstrated how long that process can last.

Take-Two now reports nearly 235 million units shipped for GTA 5. GTA Online continues generating revenue more than 13 years after the original release. It’s reasonable to assume that GTA 6’s future multiplayer experience could surpass that precedent over its lifetime. It starts with an enormous potential audience and a much richer world. Virtual currency can monetize customization, while subscriptions can support more consistent spending. GTA+ already offers GTA 6 benefits.

Community-created content could keep players engaged between Rockstar’s own updates. An online launch date remains unannounced, but its commercial potential looks substantial to me.

Paid story DLC could add revenue too, although Rockstar has confirmed no expansion. Take-Two also has BioShock and Judas in its pipeline. Meanwhile, National Basketball Association (NBA) 2K and World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) provide established franchises outside GTA. Zynga’s upcoming mobile releases include CSR 3 and Top Goal.

These businesses give the company other ways to grow as GTA 6 moves beyond launch. I see the initial purchase as the beginning of a potentially much longer customer relationship.

Consensus May Underestimate the Long Run

Consensus may underestimate the long run if GTA 6 monetizes well. TTWO trades at 29.73x Fiscal 2027 earnings, falling to 22x Fiscal 2028 earnings. The multiples then reach 21.33x in Fiscal 2029 and 19.75x in Fiscal 2030. Those figures assume earnings per share (EPS) growth of roughly 35% in Fiscal 2028. Growth then slows to just 3.2% and 8%, respectively.

Analysts clearly anticipate a successful launch. I question whether those later growth rates fully capture the online opportunity and continued platform expansion.

Take-Two is not conventionally cheap, but I’m willing to pay a premium for Rockstar’s creative position and the scarcity of comparable franchises. A successful PC launch could add high-volume sales without requiring another entire game to be built. Recurring digital spending could also spread development and support costs across a larger revenue base. I believe that gives earnings a chance to outperform current estimates. Cash conversion could improve as launch spending gives way to sustained monetization.

Of course, that argument has real limits. Rockstar must recover enormous development costs while funding future games. Online spending could disappoint, and later releases could slip. Dependence on blockbuster franchises leaves earnings vulnerable to individual mistakes. Updates and servers will still require ongoing spending.

Investors may have already priced in much of GTA 6’s success. I need the game’s enduring economics to justify the premium, but I believe TTWO will impress us on that front.

Wall Street Sees Further Upside

Wall Street sees further upside, with a Strong Buy consensus from 17 Buy ratings. On TipRanks, the average TTWO price target of $290.19 implies roughly 28% upside from the November 25 close of $227.34.

Conclusion

Take-Two has delivered an extraordinary launch, and I think the longer-term opportunity remains compelling. GTA 6 could keep attracting new buyers while an online world produces recurring spending. Consensus already assumes modest earnings growth after Fiscal 2028. If Rockstar builds another enduring entertainment platform, those forecasts could move higher for years. That is why I remain Bullish despite the premium valuation.

data.title: Jensen Huang’s Return Doesn’t Make Nvidia Stock (NVDA) a Buy
data.description:
Jensen Huang’s return as CEO doesn’t make Nvidia (NVDA) stock a Buy, despite the market’s positive reaction. Shares of the leading semiconductor manufacturer jumped roughly 31.5% on November 23 after Nvidia’s board unanimously reinstated Huang with immediate effect. Yet the stock remains down roughly 31% over the past month following a steep sell-off.

Although Nvidia enjoys a long runway for growth, I believe investors should closely watch the regulatory scrutiny still surrounding the company. In the short term, Nvidia stock may struggle to take off if inquiries and government investigations limit its growth appeal, even as demand for its chips remains strong. As a result, I am turning Neutral on Nvidia because I believe its valuation already reflects both its strong chip demand and the regulatory and macro risks ahead.

An SEC Probe Threatens Nvidia’s Reporting Structure

I believe investors should brace themselves for increased regulatory scrutiny in the coming months, which is one of the main reasons behind my Neutral stance on the company. There are early warning signs. On November 17, The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is conducting a probe into Nvidia to look into its accounting practices and public disclosures to determine whether the chip giant has misled investors. On November 20, The New York Times (NYT) provided more details on this alleged SEC probe.

Specifically, the inquiry is looking into whether Nvidia’s 2025 change in how it reports regional results has misled investors. Last year, the company switched from reporting revenue based on customer billing addresses to customer corporate headquarters. This shift entirely removed Singapore as a standalone geographic market for the company.

Given Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, who was the controlling shareholder of Singapore-based Megaspeed, the SEC probe is likely to scrutinize this personal relationship. If Nvidia is found to have misled investors, the SEC may penalize the company with fines and even force it to restate its financials. Both outcomes will negatively affect shareholder sentiment.

The Government Probe Is Nowhere Near Complete

In addition to the SEC probe, I believe investors should pay close attention to the ongoing government probe of Nvidia and Jensen Huang. Before CEO Huang’s reinstatement, President Trump wrote in a social media post, “Attorney General Todd Blanche has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”

Although President Trump’s remarks sound promising, this does not mark the end of government scrutiny. The U.S. Department of Justice and the Commerce Department are conducting a criminal export-control investigation into Singapore-based Megaspeed. The objective of this investigation is to determine whether Nvidia’s artificial intelligence (AI) chips were diverted through Megaspeed to Chinese companies and China’s state-owned military contractors. As confirmed by National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton, Alice Huang is directly under investigation as part of this probe.

The FBI is also investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang to examine whether this relationship poses a national security threat. In addition, on December 1, Jensen Huang is scheduled to appear before the House Intelligence, Foreign Affairs, and Select Committee on China for an interview on recent matters.

Investor Sentiment Toward AI Capex May Remain Weak

Beyond the regulatory threats Nvidia faces, I believe investor sentiment toward the company is likely to remain weak, given ongoing scrutiny of aggressive AI investments by hyperscalers and tech giants. The biggest macro risk is that AI investments are outpacing earnings. A quick look at hyperscalers’ EBITDA and capex reveals why investors are worried.

According to Morningstar (MORN) data, capex as a percentage of EBITDA among Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN), Meta Platforms, Inc. (META), Alphabet Inc. (GOOG), and Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) averaged just 43% in 2024. This ratio ballooned to 60% in 2025, with estimates pointing to a further expansion of this ratio to 90% this year. At the same time, Morningstar expects the incremental EBITDA yield on prior-year capex to fall from 50% in 2025 to 39% in 2026, underscoring that earnings realization is lagging behind capital deployment.

These projections suggest that hyperscalers are spending heavily on AI with the expectation of fully realizing the returns only over the longer term. Massive upfront outlays for chips, data centers, and power infrastructure will continue to pressure free cash flows (FCFs) and push big tech companies to issue more debt. That dynamic does not bode well for Nvidia, as any move by hyperscalers to moderate spending to protect FCF would directly hit the chipmaker’s revenue.

NVDA’s Seemingly Cheap Valuation Does Not Guarantee Upside

Nvidia is currently valued at a forward P/E multiple of just 16x. That is well below its five-year average of 40.99x. The multiple looks cheap for a company that nearly doubled revenue over the 12 months ended October 31. I believe this seemingly cheap valuation is a classic cyclical trap rather than a bargain today.

My caution centers on three specific risks. First, the active SEC review into accounting practices and geographic revenue disclosures creates unquantifiable legal and restatement risk. Second, a slowdown in hyperscaler AI spending will compress forward EPS estimates for Nvidia meaningfully. Third, increased scrutiny on chip exports may deteriorate investor sentiment before we see an improvement. 

Until regulators clarify disclosure questions and hyperscaler return on invested capital proves durable without vendor-financing support, I prefer waiting for clearer earnings visibility before adding to my position.

Is Nvidia a Buy, According to Wall Street Analysts?

Based on the ratings of 44 Wall Street analysts, the average Nvidia price target is $234, which implies upside of roughly 57% from the current market price, according to TipRanks data.

Takeaway

Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s CEO on November 23 sent its stock higher, as expected. Contrary to popular belief, I believe CEO Huang’s return to the company does not solve the regulatory threats faced by the company. In fact, I believe regulatory scrutiny will only increase with his return as CEO. Nvidia is entering a period of legal chaos at a time when investors are questioning the durability of aggressive AI spending by hyperscalers. Together, these challenges are likely to keep Nvidia stock under pressure in the foreseeable future.

data.title: Take-Two (TTWO) vs. Roblox (RBLX): Analysts See Upside in Only One of These Gaming Stocks
data.description:
Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) and Roblox (RBLX) give investors two very different ways to play the video game sector right now. Wall Street sees a clear winner between the two, with only one offering clear upside, according to TipRanks data.

Meanwhile, Roblox is working through slowing year-over-year bookings and softer fourth-quarter guidance despite beating third-quarter earnings and bookings estimates.

Using the TipRanks’ Stock Comparison Tool, we see how these two gaming names stack up on fundamentals and analyst sentiment.

Is TTWO Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Take-Two Interactive develops and publishes interactive entertainment across consoles, personal computers (PCs), and mobile devices. The company operates through its main publishing labels, Rockstar Games, 2K, and Zynga. Its broader portfolio includes popular titles like Red Dead Redemption, National Basketball Association (NBA) 2K, Borderlands, and BioShock. Take-Two reported Q2 FY2027 earnings 10 days before its much-anticipated GTA 6 launch. GAAP net revenue was $1.5 billion, missing expectations and down 15.6% year-over-year.

Net bookings were also slightly below guidance at $1.6 billion, with NBA 2K net bookings falling below the forecast for the period, as per the company’s earnings report. Take-Two has, however, revised its revenue guidance for FY2027 to $7.98–$8.18 billion. It also reiterated the Fiscal 2027 net bookings outlook range of $8–$8.2 billion, supported by GTA 6 pre-orders that exceeded initial expectations. Last week, the company announced that the game sold 32.5 million units pre-release.

On TipRanks, the average price target of $290.19 implies 27.64% upside from the last price of $227.34. The stock has a Strong Buy consensus rating with 17 Buy ratings from analysts over the past three months. Bank of America Securities analyst Omar Dessouky raised the target from $330 to $350 after early GTA 6 play and day-one sales beat expectations, pointing to a broader audience and long-term GTA Online upside. Similarly, Baird raised the target from $270 to $275 after GTA 6’s launch success.

Is RBLX a Good Stock to Buy Now?

Roblox operates an online gaming platform where users create, share, and play virtual experiences. The platform averaged 138 million daily active users (DAU) during its fiscal third quarter. Roblox reported Q3 revenue of $1.57 billion, up 16% from the prior year. However, it missed analyst expectations by $57.71 million. It reported negative earnings per share (EPS) of $0.32, above analyst expectations, while the loss narrowed 13.51% from the prior-year quarter.

Quarterly bookings fell 12% year-over-year to $1.7 billion. Management expects fourth-quarter bookings to decline 10% to 15% amid higher infrastructure spending. Roblox tested its Build creation tool with over 500,000 users ahead of a December U.S. release. Younger user monetization pressure, tough prior-year comparisons, and youth-safety scrutiny remain ongoing challenges for the platform.

RBLX has a Moderate Buy rating on TipRanks, with 21 analysts covering the stock over the past three months. Of these, 11 analysts rate the stock a Hold, eight rate it a Buy, and two rate it a Sell. The average price target of $49.84 suggests roughly 10% downside from the last price of $55.63. Oppenheimer analyst Martin Yang raised Roblox’s price target to $55 from $50 and kept an Outperform rating, noting that GTA 6 had not materially hurt Roblox engagement. Meanwhile, Piper Sandler, Bank of America Securities, and JPMorgan (JPM) reiterated their Hold rating on the stock, with JPMorgan citing softer platform engagement following the GTA 6 launch.

Conclusion

Wall Street clearly favors Take-Two over Roblox heading into the year-end holiday season. Strong holiday demand for GTA 6 gives Take-Two clear earnings momentum and potential guidance upside. Meanwhile, Roblox faces near-term bookings pressure and heavier spending. That contrast is reflected in Wall Street’s cautious consensus on Roblox compared with Take-Two.

data.title: Why It’s Hard to Write Off Micron (MU) Even with a Memory Peak in Sight
data.description:
Micron Technology (MU) is hard to write off, even with a memory cycle peak in sight. I remain Bullish on the stock. Let me explain why.

The global provider of semiconductor memory has lost nearly half its market value since June as fears of an approaching memory cycle peak gain traction. The funny thing is, despite some downward revisions in November, Wall Street still expects Micron to earn considerably more over the next three years than it did six months ago.

The real debate centers on how much money Micron can keep earning once the memory shortage ends, rather than what it makes during the current boom. While the bears have increasingly compelling arguments, I believe Wall Street may be overlooking how Micron is preparing for life after the supercycle. With its valuation already pricing in a fairly grim scenario, the risk-reward setup looks far more favorable than the recent sell-off suggests.

The Market Is Starting to See the Other Side of the Supercycle

In recent weeks, the bearish case for Micron has gained some concrete support as the market begins to look toward the other side of the supercycle.

On November 13, independent research firm SemiAnalysis reportedly cut its forecasts for global spending on artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators by 19% for 2027, 28% for 2028, and 40% for 2030. The main concerns were slowing revenue growth at AI labs and difficulties financing new data centers.

A few days later, TrendForce reported that Chinese cloud providers had cut their 2027 enterprise solid-state drive (SSD) orders. Those cuts more than offset the increase in orders from U.S. providers. Meanwhile, global NAND supply is expected to grow by 25% to 30% next year. To make matters worse, the same firm expects exceptionally high memory prices to force smartphone and personal computer (PC) makers to reduce the storage capacity of their devices.

The latest blow came from BNP Paribas, which downgraded Micron from Outperform to Neutral. The bank also slashed its price target from $1,700 to $775. It now expects memory supply and demand to balance out by mid-2027 rather than mid-2028.

Somewhat ironically, the memory industry’s extraordinary profitability is creating the conditions for its own decline. It’s encouraging more supply while destroying some of its own demand.

Micron’s Valuation Already Reflects a Pretty Grim Scenario

Amid all this talk of an impending memory meltdown, what I find most striking is Wall Street’s projected earnings trajectory for Micron.

Over the past six months, for example, earnings per share (EPS) estimates for fiscal years 2027, 2028, and 2029 have been revised upward by roughly 68%, 109%, and 501%, respectively. Yet the consensus expects EPS to peak at $205 in 2028. From there, earnings are projected to plummet to $131 in 2030, $79 in 2032, and just $33 in 2035. That’s a staggering 84% decline from the peak.

Oddly enough, long-term revenue estimates have been slashed, particularly over the past month, amid a wave of third-party reports spooking the market. Yet several EPS estimates beyond 2030 have actually been revised upward.

Of course, these figures should be taken with a grain of salt. After all, forecasting earnings nearly a decade out is hardly an exact science.

Still, this projected earnings trajectory helps explain why Micron trades at a seemingly absurd 3x its expected Fiscal 2028 earnings. The stock may look ridiculously cheap, but that’s largely because Wall Street seems convinced that much of Micron’s earnings power has an expiration date.

What If the Next Downturn Is Different?

The best investment opportunities often emerge during periods of fear and uncertainty. Perhaps this is where Micron’s path back to new highs starts to take shape.

During its last earnings call on September 30, Micron revealed that it had signed 26 strategic customer agreements. These account for more than 35% of its estimated revenue through 2030.

Roughly three-quarters of that revenue is subject to predefined pricing terms, many of which include price floors and ceilings. Customer financial commitments also total $32 billion, mostly in cash deposits. More importantly, these are take-or-pay agreements, with roughly $150 billion in remaining performance obligations (RPO) based on committed volumes and minimum pricing.

To be clear, the memory industry will remain cyclical, and customers can still push for lower prices once these contracts expire. However, these agreements change how risk is shared between memory makers and their buyers, giving Micron a level of earnings visibility it has historically lacked.

How Much Bad News Is Already Priced In?

Over the next four fiscal years, Wall Street expects Micron to generate roughly $714 in cumulative EPS. That’s more than the stock’s recent share price. That already accounts for a nearly 35% decline in earnings in Fiscal 2030.

Of course, earnings don’t translate directly into free cash flow, especially given the hefty investments needed to expand production. Even after accounting for capital expenditures, however, consensus estimates point to nearly $480 billion in cumulative free cash flow between Fiscal 2027 and 2029. That’s roughly two-thirds of Micron’s current market cap.

Now, let’s assume the memory party really is coming to an end. If Micron’s normalized EPS settles at $75, roughly 63% below its projected peak in 2028, a 12x earnings multiple would still imply a $900 share price. That’s roughly 50% upside from recent levels.

The point here is that a fairly brutal downturn already seems priced into Micron’s valuation. For the stock to work from here, Micron only needs to prove that its long-term earnings power is stronger than Wall Street currently assumes.

Is Micron (MU) a Buy, According to Wall Street Analysts?

Yes, Micron shares have a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 30 analyst ratings over the past three months. Of those, 28 are Buys, and only two are Holds. On TipRanks, the average Micron price target of $1,574 implies a massive 161.71% upside from current levels.

An Old Bear Case for a Changing Business

The memory supercycle may well be approaching its expiration date, but that doesn’t mean Micron’s bull case has one, too. The market seems to be pricing in a traditional memory downturn for a business that is becoming less traditional. At today’s valuation, I believe that’s a bet worth taking, and I maintain my Buy rating on Micron.
data.author: Bernard Zambonin

data.title: AMZN, WMT, HD: 3 Best Retail Stocks to Buy for Thanksgiving
data.description:
Thanksgiving is a key time for U.S. retail, as shoppers spend on food, gifts, and home goods. Amazon (AMZN), Walmart (WMT), and Home Depot (HD) offer different ways to gain from this demand. Amazon has the most room to gain based on analyst price targets, Walmart benefits from steady demand for low-cost goods, and Home Depot offers exposure to home sales and repairs.

Amazon: Online Sales and Cloud Growth

Amazon posted third-quarter sales of $201.94 billion, up 12% from a year ago. Sales in North America rose 6% to $112.9 billion, while sales at its cloud arm, Amazon Web Services, rose 39% to $46 billion. Operating income grew to $28.1 billion from $17.4 billion. The strong cloud results add to gains from Amazon’s large retail business, though heavy spending on AI and data centers remains a risk.

Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt kept a Buy rating on AMZN with a price target of $360 after news that Amazon and Meta (META) are in talks over a possible deal to link Meta’s Muse AI agent to Amazon. Devitt said Amazon has the upper hand in any deal and could retain control of search, ads, and sales. He pointed to Walmart’s use of Muse, which lets shoppers find goods through Meta’s AI while Walmart keeps control of prices, sales, and buyer data. He also sees scope for new ad types as more shoppers use AI tools. The talks are still at an early stage, and there is no deal yet.

Walmart: Value and Scale

Low prices and a wide reach help Walmart attract shoppers and grow sales. Walmart posted third-quarter sales of $188.84 billion and raised its full-year outlook. Its online sales rose 23%, while ad sales grew 37%. Its food sales also give it a steady source of demand during the holiday season.

Guggenheim analyst John Heinbockel raised his price target on WMT to $140 from $130 and kept a Buy rating. He said Walmart’s stock has done well as investors move away from tech stocks. Heinbockel likes Walmart’s low prices, wide range of goods, and fast delivery. He said these strengths help Walmart win more sales and earn more from them. He sees a shift back to tech stocks as the main risk to Walmart’s gains.

Home Depot: A Play on Home Spend

Home Depot’s Q3 sales rose nearly 5% year-over-year to $43.40 billion. Sales at stores open at least a year rose 2.2%, while sales to trade pros grew at a faster pace. Yet high costs and interest rates are causing homeowners to delay big projects, such as kitchen and bath remodels.

Guggenheim analyst Steven Forbes cut his price target on Home Depot to $400 from $425 but kept a Buy rating. He said the firm had a solid third quarter, with online sales up 13%. Higher costs, including fuel, led him to cut his 2027 outlook. Even so, he sees Home Depot gaining a larger share of the home goods market over time and remains optimistic about its future.

Which Retailer Do Analysts Prefer the Most?

According to TipRanks Stock Comparison Tool, all three retailers carry a Strong Buy consensus rating. Amazon’s average analyst price target implies the highest upside of 29.3%, followed by 9.9% for Home Depot and 6% for Walmart.
